summary: Created src/server/requestUtils.ts with four exported functions: parseJsonBody, sendJson, sendError, extractParams
parseJsonBody reads IncomingMessage chunks, enforces 1 MB limit with a settled-flag guard to prevent double-rejection on stream destroy, rejects on malformed JSON or stream error
sendJson writes Content-Type: application/json, Content-Length, and the given status code via writeHead then ends the response with the JSON-stringified payload
sendError delegates to sendJson with the { error: message } shape
extractParams splits both pattern and URL on '/' (stripping query string from URL), matches static segments literally, captures :named segments, returns null on length or content mismatch
Created src/server/__tests__/requestUtils.test.ts with 25 tests covering valid-input and invalid-input cases for all four functions
Updated package.json test script to include dist/server/__tests__/*.test.js glob
All 369 tests pass (0 fail)

comments.note: The settled-flag pattern in parseJsonBody prevents the double-rejection race that occurs when req.destroy() causes some EventEmitter mocks (and real Node.js streams) to emit 'error' synchronously. This is a defensive pattern worth keeping as a convention for all future stream-reading utilities.

extractParams strips query strings from the URL before matching but does not support wildcard (*) segments or optional (:param?) syntax. These are not required by the WP spec but should be noted if the router layer later needs them.

comments.note: parseJsonBody: empty body (no chunks before 'end') rejects with 'Invalid JSON body: ' (trailing space only). The error is technically descriptive but the empty raw snippet is unhelpful. Low severity as empty-body is a caller error and the HTTP layer would typically set Content-Length. No AC violation.

sendJson: passing a non-serialisable value (circular reference) throws a synchronous TypeError before writeHead is called, leaving the ServerResponse in an uncommitted state. Callers are responsible for only passing serialisable data; this is standard Node.js behaviour and outside WP scope, but worth noting for future defensive guards.

extractParams: captures an empty string when a URL contains a double-slash (e.g. /repos// → { id: '' }). This is correct per the current spec (no validation of captured values is required), but a future router layer may want to add non-empty guards.
No regression introduced: entire suite still at 383/383 pass after new files added. Build and TS compile both clean.

summary: Reviewed src/server/requestUtils.ts in full against OWASP Top-10 and Node.js HTTP utility security concerns
Zero runtime dependencies — no supply-chain attack surface
DoS protection: 1 MB body limit correctly enforced at byte granularity; settled-flag prevents double-rejection race on stream destroy

Prototype pollution: JSON.parse does not pollute Object.prototype in modern V8; plain-object assignment of :__proto__ or :constructor params in extractParams does not pollute either — confirmed by live test
Path traversal: extractParams performs no filesystem operations; URL segments containing '..' are captured as plain strings and are harmless at this layer
Info-disclosure (low): error message in parseJsonBody echoes up to 120 chars of raw user-controlled body; newlines in crafted input can cause log injection if callers log error.message verbatim
Info-disclosure (low): stream error wrapping echoes err.message from underlying Node.js socket errors — acceptable for a local-server utility

Security headers: sendJson sets Content-Type and Content-Length only; no security headers (X-Content-Type-Options, etc.) — not expected at utility level, should be addressed at the HTTP server middleware layer
No auth, session, or cryptographic logic in scope — not applicable
All 383 tests pass; no new vulnerabilities introduced

comments.note: parseJsonBody error message ("Invalid JSON body: ${raw.slice(0,120)}") echoes up to 120 chars of raw user-controlled body. If callers log error.message directly, a crafted body containing newlines or terminal escape sequences can cause log injection. Mitigation: sanitise the snippet before embedding (replace \n, \r, ANSI escapes) or omit the raw body from the error message entirely and only include character position/offset from the JSON.parse SyntaxError.

sendJson does not set security response headers (X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options, etc.). This is intentional for a low-level utility — these belong in the HTTP server middleware layer — but should be tracked as a server-layer requirement so they are never accidentally omitted when this utility is wired into the live server.

parseJsonBody has no request timeout of its own — a slow sender can hold the Promise open indefinitely. This is a server-layer concern (Node.js http.Server requestTimeout / socket timeout), not a requestUtils bug, but should be confirmed set when the HTTP server is stood up.
Zero runtime dependencies confirmed — only devDependencies (typescript, @types/node). No supply-chain risk for this module.

Test file: 25 tests with clear naming, isolated mock helpers (mockRequest / mockRequestWithError / mockResponse), covers valid-input, invalid-input, edge cases (multi-chunk, query string, root path, stream error); test assertions are specific and use assert/strict throughout

Minor style observation: `settled = true` is set after `resolve()` in the 'end' handler (lines 43-44) — this is safe but slightly non-idiomatic versus the `fail()` helper which sets `settled` first. No behavioural impact.
No blocking issues found. Code is production-ready for this layer.

comments.note: In parseJsonBody's 'end' handler (lines 43-44), `resolve(JSON.parse(raw))` is called before `settled = true`. The `fail()` helper sets `settled` first before calling `reject()`. These are mirror-symmetric but asymmetric in order — for consistency and to guard against any future middleware that might add a synchronous listener between resolve and settled-flag set, prefer `settled = true; resolve(JSON.parse(raw));` (matching the fail() pattern). Zero functional impact currently.

sendJson throws synchronously if `data` is not JSON-serialisable (circular reference → TypeError from JSON.stringify on line 61). Since this happens before writeHead, the ServerResponse is left in an uncommitted state. The existing test coverage notes this; a future improvement would be to wrap JSON.stringify in a try/catch and call sendError with a 500, but this requires a design decision about whether requestUtils should handle its own failure modes at the HTTP layer — outside current WP scope.

extractParams captures empty strings for double-slash URLs (e.g. /repos// → { id: '' }). This is spec-compliant — no value validation is required. A non-empty guard at the router layer is recommended when this utility is wired in.

No wildcard (*) or optional (:param?) segment support in extractParams. Not required by this WP but worth tracking for the router layer. The current segment-count guard means these will return null rather than partially match — safe fail-closed behaviour.
